subject.title: fix(acp): close shared state database on ACP server shutdown

question: Should maintainers repair this focused ACP shutdown PR as the canonical fix for the SQLite handle leak, or prefer the broader process-global SQLite cache lifecycle path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100827?
rationale: Multiple active PRs split the fix between per-server shutdown wiring, ledger lifecycle, and process-global cache ownership; choosing the permanent owner boundary is not safely mechanical.

options.title: Prefer owner-level cache lifecycle
options.body: Use the broader SQLite cache-owner direction if maintainers want cleanup to happen at the process-global handle owner rather than in each server shutdown path.

options.title: Repair this focused PR
options.body: Track, drain, or cancel ACP gateway event handlers before closing the shared DB, then add real ACP shutdown proof and make this the canonical small fix.

options.title: Choose a ledger-lifecycle sibling
options.body: Use a sibling PR only if maintainers want `AcpEventLedger` to grow an explicit close contract and that branch also prevents late writes after close.

recommendation.title: Prefer owner-level cache lifecycle
recommendation.body: Use the broader SQLite cache-owner direction if maintainers want cleanup to happen at the process-global handle owner rather than in each server shutdown path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and ACP SQLite history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the lifecycle-boundary choice.
